name: Panther Habit
summary: The ceremonial suit of Wakanda's king, laced with vibranium, the metal that soaks up impact. It grew from a simple cowl and cape into armour that can store a blow and hit back with it.

parts.label: Mask
parts.fact: Kirby's first cover for Fantastic Four #52 showed a cowl with the face exposed; it was printed as a full mask. Modern masks add comms and lenses that see UV and infrared.

parts.label: Kinetic chest
parts.fact: On film, the nanite suit Shuri designs in Black Panther (2018) drinks in the force of a strike, glows purple along its patterned lines, then dumps that energy back out in a blast.

parts.label: Claws
parts.fact: Later comics give the finger gauntlets razor-sharp claws, so the king is never unarmed even when he carries no separate weapon.

parts.label: Soles
parts.fact: In the comics, vibranium threaded through the boot soles soaks up the shock of impacts, so long drops and hard landings barely jar him.

parts.label: Back (cape gone)
parts.fact: Kirby's earliest version of the costume had a cape and collar; he soon trimmed both away, leaving the clean all-black silhouette the character still wears.

parts.label: Vibranium weave
parts.fact: Wakandan vibranium, introduced in Fantastic Four #53 (1966), absorbs vibration and kinetic energy. Writers Priest and Hudlin drew the suit as bulletproof armour.

trivia: Kirby's first concept for the hero was a swashbuckler named the Coal Tiger before Stan Lee asked for changes.
In the 1970s Jungle Action series, artists gave T'Challa a gold-chain look inspired by Isaac Hayes's outfit in Wattstax (1973).
On film, the suit concept came from Marvel designer Ryan Meinerding, with the triangle-patterned details worked out by Ruth E. Carter's costume team.
Ruth E. Carter won the Academy Award for costume design for Black Panther, and a suit worn by Chadwick Boseman is in the Smithsonian's collection.
The habit's live-action debut came in Captain America: Civil War (2016).
